title: WPSB/113/2016 of Shiv Charan Vs Union Of India AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (SB) No. 113 of 2016
Shiv Charan ......... Petitioner
 Versus
Union of India and others. ......... Respondents
Mr. Lok Pal Singh, Mr. Ashish Srivastava and Mr. Prabhat Bohra, Advocates for the
petitioner.
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Assistant Solicitor General for Union of India/ respondent nos. 1 to 4.
Date: 16th March, 2016
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
 Petitioner challenges Annexure-11. Petitioner is an
applicant in O.A., which was filed before the Central
Administrative Tribunal, Circuit Bench at Nainital. He has
obtained an order restraining promotions being made. One Rajesh
Kumar Tiwari, i.e. respondent no. 13 had approached this Court
feeling aggrieved by the order restraining promotions being made.
This Court, by Annexure-2 order, disposed of the matter by
directing that respondent no. 13 can approach for vacation /
modification / clarification of the interim order and also for
having the matter heard before the Allahabad Bench. It appears
that his Intervention Application was allowed and he was
impleaded as a respondent. The matter was to be heard finally by
the Nainital Bench. It is while so that the Application was moved
by respondent no. 12 seeking to invoke powers of the Chairman
under Section 25 of the Central Administrative Tribunal Act 1985
(hereinafter referred to as the Act), which reads as follows:

2
"[25. Power of Chairman to transfer cases from one
Bench to another.-On the application of any of the
parties and after notice to the parties, and after hearing such
of them as he may desire to be heard, or on his own motion
without such notice, the Chairman may transfer any case
pending before one Bench, for disposal, to any other
Bench.]"
2. The Chairman, in purported exercise of the power
under Section 25 of the Act, has deemed it fit to allow the
Application. Hence, the writ petition.
3. We heard Mr. Lok Pal Singh, learned counsel
appearing on behalf of the petitioner and Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal on
behalf of the official respondents.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner Mr. Lok Pal Singh,
no doubt, contended that the Chairman may not have unfettered
power under Section 25 of the Act and this approach to the
problem has been disclosed in an order passed by the Chairman
himself. He would submit that the petitioner would be put to the
pain of engaging another lawyer at Delhi. He further submits that
his role as dominus litis, which is also recognized by the
Chairman in the other order, does not appear to find reflection in
this order. We must remind ourselves that we are acting in
judicial review. There is no case for the petitioner that there is no
power with the Chairman to transfer it from Nainital to Delhi.
From the order, we notice that except for the petitioner, all the
other parties are agreeable for the case being heard at the Principal
Bench, which is located at Delhi. As far as petitioner being
dominus litis, it is not as if the Chairman has not considered the
said issue; the Chairman takes the view that the distance from
Dehradun to Nainital is almost the same as the distance from
Dehradun to Delhi. Therefore, it is not as if it is a cryptic order
without giving any reason. As to the sufficiency of the reasons in
judicial review, the court would not be justified in substituting its

3
views for the view taken by the Authority under Section 25 of the
Act.
5. In such circumstances, we would think that no case is
made out. The writ petition is dismissed. No order as to costs.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 16.03.2016 16.03.2016
Rathour
